name: Xfinity (Comcast) Internet
notes: Researched from public xfinity.com support articles only (no sign-in). Sign-in uses an Xfinity ID, which can be an email address, mobile number or username; optional two-step verification sends a one-time code by text or email (or a push/code generator), so mfa is email_or_sms. Review 2026-10-09: the public sign-in page (login.xfinity.com/login) was observed in a browser: one field "Email, mobile, or username" with a Let's go button (password on the next step), plus Find your Xfinity ID and Create a new Xfinity ID links, so loginSteps 2 is observed. One-time payments: Billing & Pay > Make a Payment, Current balance or Pay another amount, a payment date, saved or new bank account/card (new methods need a six-digit code; banks verified via Plaid), Continue, Submit Payment. Paying online requires signing in (Quick Pay without sign-in was retired for home services; forum staff statements), so guest_pay is unsupported (inferred); the staff post lists bank bill pay and the Voice Remote, and replies add mail and store kiosks. Paying by phone at 1-800-XFINITY is not stated on the official pages reviewed (number from the cancel page), so pay_by_phone is inferred. Auto Pay (Billing & Pay > Manage Auto Pay > Set Up / Turn Off) drafts the current balance on the bill due date from checking, savings or a card; it can't be turned off on a day a payment is processing. The $10/month Auto Pay + Paperless discount needs Xfinity Internet and a stored bank account (cards no longer qualify). Payment arrangements and the bill assistance plan are offered through Xfinity Assistant chat when eligible; the engine models them as the family installments form. Cancelling is by phone, a scheduled call or an Xfinity Store (no self-service online cancel). Fees: no online payment fee is published, so fees are left out. Plan prices vary by market and are not modelled.

guest_pay.note: Online payments need you to sign in with your Xfinity ID (Quick Pay was retired). Without signing in, pay through your bank's bill pay, by mail, at a kiosk in an Xfinity Store, or by calling 1-800-XFINITY.

autopay_cancel.note: Auto Pay can't be turned off on a day when a payment is already processing.

cancel_service.note: Xfinity services can't be cancelled online. Call 1-800-XFINITY (1-800-934-6489), schedule a call, or visit an Xfinity Store.

help.title: Ways to pay your bill
paragraphs: To pay online, sign in with the Primary or Manager Xfinity ID, open Billing & Pay and choose Make a Payment. Pick Current balance or Pay another amount, choose a payment date, then a saved method or a new U.S. checking or savings account or an American Express, Discover, Mastercard or Visa card. Select Continue, review, and choose Submit Payment. Keep the confirmation and authorization numbers.
Adding a new method asks for a six-digit code sent to your phone or email, and new bank accounts are verified through Plaid.

You must sign in to pay online; Xfinity retired its no-sign-in Quick Pay. Without signing in you can add Xfinity as a payee in your bank's bill pay, mail a check, pay at a self-service kiosk in an Xfinity Store, or call 1-800-XFINITY.
steps: Sign in with your Xfinity ID.
Open Billing & Pay and choose Make a Payment.
Choose the amount and payment date.
Pick or add a payment method and select Continue.

help.title: Set up or turn off Auto Pay
paragraphs: Auto Pay charges your current balance (your bill minus credits and recent payments) on the bill due date. It can take up to three business days to process. You can use a checking account, a savings account, or a credit or debit card.

To turn it off, open Billing & Pay, choose Manage Auto Pay, select Turn Off and confirm. You can't turn it off on a day when a payment is processing. Xfinity Mobile requires Auto Pay, so there you can only change the payment method.
steps: Sign in and open Billing & Pay.
Pick a payment method and accept the Automatic Payments Terms & Conditions.

help.title: Auto Pay and Paperless Billing discount
paragraphs: Xfinity Internet customers can get $10 off each month by enrolling in both Auto Pay and Paperless Billing with a stored bank account. Debit and credit cards no longer qualify for the discount.

The discount begins within 45 days and may take up to two bills to show. You lose it if you remove Auto Pay or Paperless Billing, cancel Xfinity Internet, switch Auto Pay to a card, or an automatic payment fails (which also unenrolls you from Auto Pay). Business accounts are not eligible.

help.title: Turn on Paperless Billing
paragraphs: Only the primary user or a manager can turn on Paperless Billing. Online, open Billing & Pay, choose Manage Paperless Billing and select Turn On. In the Xfinity app, go to Account, Bill details, Bill settings, then Paperless billing.
If you receive Xfinity bills through your bank's online bill service, unenroll there first.
steps: Sign in and open Billing & Pay.

help.title: Payment arrangements and bill assistance
paragraphs: If you qualify, a flexible-payment message appears when you sign in. Select Chat for options to open Xfinity Assistant, choose the payment arrangement, pick a payment date and submit.

Customers with Xfinity Internet for at least a year may qualify for a bill assistance plan: a temporary monthly credit for six months, as long as service is not disconnected for non-payment. Any past-due balance must be paid or put on an installment plan first, and the credit shows within two bill cycles.

help.title: Cancel Xfinity service
paragraphs: Xfinity services are cancelled by calling 1-800-934-6489, scheduling a call, or visiting an Xfinity Store; there is no self-service cancellation online. Xfinity Mobile customers should transfer their number before cancelling. NOW Internet is managed in its own portal.

extra.intent: Using the Xfinity support pages, find how much the monthly Auto Pay and Paperless Billing discount is for Xfinity Internet and which payment method qualifies. Do not make a payment or change any settings.

solution.text: The discount is $10 per month and needs Auto Pay plus Paperless Billing with a stored bank account; cards no longer qualify.

extra.intent: A customer wants the Xfinity Auto Pay and Paperless discount while paying Auto Pay with a credit card. Check the Xfinity help pages and say whether a card qualifies, naming the payment method that does. Do not change any settings.

solution.text: No. Only a stored bank account qualifies for the discount; debit and credit cards no longer do.
